homePage.openSectionPara1: In July 2026 Ryan Fox won The 154th Open at Royal Birkdale with a birdie on the 72nd hole, finishing on 10 under par, one shot ahead of Cameron Young. It was Birkdale's 11th Open since 1954, on a course where Tom Watson won his fifth Claret Jug in 1983 and Jordan Spieth won in 2017.
homePage.openSectionPara2: Royal Birkdale says its visitor tee times are fully booked through 2026 and 2027. The other Sefton Coast courses take visitors, except Hillside until mid-March 2027, and the course guides below set out how each one books.

homePage.editorialPara1: There are links golf corridors in Scotland: St Andrews, Carnoustie, Muirfield: that get the attention. The Sefton Coast gets overlooked. That gap is the opportunity for every visiting golfer.
homePage.editorialPara2: On one stretch of coastline there are six links courses, from Royal Birkdale to Southport Old Links. You can play a different course every day for a week and the ground changes each time. Birkdale through dramatic willow scrub dunes. Hillside through ridge-and-valley terrain. Formby through coastal pinewoods. West Lancashire with raw Irish Sea exposure.
homePage.editorialPara3: The practical case is simple: the coast is within reach of Liverpool and Manchester airports, and the six courses sit close together, so you can play a different one each day without long transfers.
homePage.editorialPara4: Royal Birkdale has hosted The Open 11 times, most recently in July 2026, when Ryan Fox won with a birdie on the final hole. Tom Watson won his fifth Claret Jug there in 1983 and Jordan Spieth won in 2017. If you have ever thought about a links golf trip to England, this coast is a good place to start.
homePage.featureCard1Text: 45 min from Liverpool Airport, 60 min from Manchester. Direct rail to Southport from Liverpool city centre.
homePage.featureCard2Text: West Lancashire, Formby, Southport & Ainsdale and Southport Old Links take visitor bookings. Royal Birkdale is fully booked for visitors through 2027, and Hillside is closed to visitors until mid-March 2027.
homePage.featureCard3Text: From November 2026 to February 2027, West Lancashire charges £120 per person on weekdays and Formby £155 on weekdays.

open.summary: Eleven Opens since 1954. Ryan Fox won the 154th in July 2026.

openPage.aboutTitle: The Open Championship at Royal Birkdale
openPage.aboutPara1: Royal Birkdale has hosted The Open 11 times, from 1954 to 2026. Since first hosting it in 1954, Birkdale has been the Championship's most regular venue apart from St Andrews. The club was founded in 1889, and the course was extensively redesigned in 1922 to create the current layout, which winds between sand dunes that tower over the fairways.
openPage.aboutPara2: The 154th Open ran from 12 to 19 July 2026, with four practice days from Sunday to Wednesday and the Championship from Thursday to Sunday. Ryan Fox of New Zealand won with rounds of 72, 68, 62 and 68 for 270, 10 under par, one shot ahead of Cameron Young, with Sam Burns third. Fox was level par at halfway, equalled the lowest round in Open history with a third-round 62, and birdied the 72nd hole to win. It was his first major title, and he became the second New Zealander to be Champion Golfer of the Year. The club says more than 300,000 spectators came through the gates during the week.
openPage.aboutPara3: The 2017 Open had one of the great finishes. Jordan Spieth led after each of the first three rounds, fell one behind Matt Kuchar after an eventful 13th hole in the final round, then went birdie, eagle, birdie, birdie from the 14th to win by three on 12 under par.
openPage.aboutPara4: Besides its 11 Opens, the club lists two Ryder Cups (1965 and 1969), six Women's Opens, the Senior Open in 2013, the Walker Cup in 1951 and the Curtis Cup in 1948 among the championships it has staged.
openPage.champNote2017: Birdie, eagle, birdie, birdie from the 14th to win by three
openPage.champNote1998: Won a four-hole play-off for his second major of 1998
openPage.champNote1971: The 100th Open: his third win in four weeks, after the U.S. and Canadian Opens
openPage.champNote1961: 6-iron from the base of a bush at the 15th, now the 16th

teeTimesPage.formbyCalloutTitle: Formby Golf Club: How Visiting Works
teeTimesPage.formbyCalloutIntro: Formby sets out its visitor arrangements on its own website. In summary:
teeTimesPage.formbyPoint1Text: The club says it welcomes visitors from all over the globe. Saturday and Sunday are members' competition days.
teeTimesPage.formbyPoint2Text: Visitor tee times can be booked online from the club's website, or by calling 01704 872164 or emailing teetimes@formbygolfclub.co.uk.
teeTimesPage.formbyPoint3Text: Visitors are asked to bring a current recognised handicap certificate. The maximum handicap is 28 for men and 36 for women.
teeTimesPage.formbyPoint4Text: From November 2026 to March 2027 the club warns of occasional disruption, including temporary greens, bunker closures or a shorter course.
teeTimesPage.formbyPoint5Text: £155 Monday to Friday and £175 at weekends from November 2026 to February 2027. From April to September 2027, £320 on weekdays and £350 at weekends.
teeTimesPage.formbyPoint6Text: The club has a small fleet of buggies for hire on medical grounds only. Show a medical certificate at the Professional Shop.
teeTimesPage.handicapRequirementText: Men's certificate required (limit {limit}). Bring your club handicap card or EGA card.
teeTimesPage.tip1Text: All courses on the Sefton Coast except Southport Old Links require a handicap certificate. Your national golf association card or EGA card is accepted.
teeTimesPage.tip2Text: Royal Birkdale is fully booked for visitors through 2027, and Hillside is closed to visitors until mid-March 2027. Southport & Ainsdale says May, June, July and September are in great demand, with many overseas visitors booking several years ahead.
teeTimesPage.tip3Text: Smart casual minimum at all clubs. No denim, no trainers, no t-shirts at most. Some clubs require collar and tailored trousers in the clubhouse.
teeTimesPage.tip4Text: Links courses often require a walk from car park to first tee. You want time to warm up and ask the pro shop about local rules and any temporary conditions.
teeTimesPage.tip5Title: Ask about the drop zone system
teeTimesPage.tip5Text: Royal Birkdale has specific drop zones and areas of special interest under local rules. Get the local rules card from the pro shop.
teeTimesPage.tip6Title: Weather changes fast on the coast
teeTimesPage.tip6Text: Pack a waterproof even if the morning looks clear. Coastal weather is unpredictable. A SW wind that's fresh in the morning can be strong by the back nine.

accommodationPage.pageDesc: Hotels and areas to stay near Royal Birkdale and the other Sefton Coast courses, with what each hotel's own website lists.
accommodationPage.tip1: Book Tuesday–Thursday tee times if staying mid-week: better availability at all courses and usually quieter on the course.
accommodationPage.tip2: Ask about club/bag storage when booking. Good golf hotels will have a dedicated dry store rather than leaving bags in your room overnight.
accommodationPage.tip3: Birkdale station (Merseyrail) is an 8-minute walk from Royal Birkdale's main entrance. Useful if your hotel is in central Southport.
accommodationPage.tip4: Flexible cancellation matters: links golf weather is unpredictable. Book refundable rates unless the savings on non-refundable are significant.

scorecardPage.slopeRatingDesc: Measures difficulty relative to a bogey golfer. The USGA scale runs from 55 to 155: a slope of 113 is average, 148 (Royal Birkdale championship) is extremely difficult.
scorecardPage.yardageMetresDesc: English clubs use yards. Metres are provided for continental European visitors. GPS devices and rangefinders are widely permitted: check with each club before use in competitions.

itinerariesPage.howToPlanTitle: How to Plan a Sefton Coast Golf Trip
itinerariesPage.howToPlanPara1: The Sefton Coast courses are clustered enough that a two-day trip can cover two or three rounds without difficult logistics. Royal Birkdale and Hillside are literally adjacent: you could walk between them. Southport & Ainsdale is three miles further south. Formby is five miles from Birkdale via the A565.
itinerariesPage.howToPlanPara2: For multi-day trips, base yourself in Southport. The town has the widest hotel choice, and everything from Lord Street to Birkdale is within taxi distance. If you want quieter and cheaper accommodation, Formby village is 20 minutes south and has decent B&B options.
itinerariesPage.howToPlanPara3: Plan around the season. Saturday and Sunday are members' competition days at Formby, and the clubs do most of their course work between November and March, so ask about temporary greens, mats or a shorter course when you book.
itinerariesPage.howToPlanPara4: Book tee times before you arrive. Royal Birkdale says its visitor tee times are fully booked through 2027, and Hillside is closed to visitors for winter maintenance until mid-March 2027. Formby, West Lancashire, Southport & Ainsdale and Southport Old Links all take bookings online.

conditionsPage.aboutLinksPara1: Links golf conditions are fundamentally different from parkland golf. The key variables are wind direction and strength, recent rainfall and drainage, and the firmness of the turf. A firm, dry course plays completely differently to a wet, soft one: approach shots don't stop, the ball runs further off the tee, and chipping becomes more creative.
conditionsPage.aboutLinksPara2: The Sefton Coast courses are built on sand, so they usually drain faster than inland courses after heavy rain. Each club posts its own course status: check it before you travel.
conditionsPage.aboutLinksPara3: Wind speed and direction matter more here than almost anywhere in England. The prevailing south-westerly at Royal Birkdale creates the 'natural' course experience the routing was designed for. An easterly off the land produces a completely different course. This guide includes a wind direction key for Royal Birkdale specifically.

royal-birkdale.tagline: Eleven Opens since 1954; Ryan Fox won the 154th here in 2026
royal-birkdale.description:
Royal Birkdale sits among towering sand dunes in Southport. It hosted The Open for the 11th time in July 2026, when Ryan Fox won with a birdie on the 72nd hole.

The club was founded in 1889, and the course was extensively redesigned in 1922 to create the current layout, which winds between sand dunes that tower over the fairways. The club offers four tee options, from 4,877 to 6,736 yards, and asks golfers who want to play the longest tees to get approval from its office.

The club says its visitor tee times are fully booked throughout 2026 and 2027, including its Birkdale Open Experience Package, and asks golfers to check its website for 2028 availability.
royal-birkdale.visitorPolicy: The club says visitor tee times are fully booked throughout 2026 and 2027, including its Birkdale Open Experience Package. Check its website for 2028 availability.

hillside.tagline: Links golf next door to Royal Birkdale
hillside.description:
Hillside sits immediately next to Royal Birkdale and shares the same duneland. The club's green fee table lists its winter rate as closed for maintenance from 19 October 2026 to mid-March 2027. Its spring rate starts in March 2027.

From 1960 the club rebuilt several holes, including the 11th, 16th and 17th, through valleys in the taller dunes. Its practice ground served as the official practice ground for The 154th Open at Royal Birkdale in 2026, and the club has staged DP World Tour events and R&A championships.
hillside.visitorPolicy: Closed to visitors for winter maintenance from 19 October 2026 to mid-March 2027. Visitor enquiries go to the Secretary's Office.

formby.tagline: Founded in 1884: a championship links among dunes and pine trees
formby.description:
Formby Golf Club was founded in 1884 and describes itself as a true championship links, with mature sand dunes, undulating fairways, well-protected greens and views of the Irish Sea. Visitors can book online. Saturday and Sunday are members' competition days.

The club has hosted the Amateur Championship and the PGA Seniors Championship. Its clubhouse has bars and dining, snooker tables and en-suite Dormy accommodation.
formby.visitorPolicy: Visitors welcome. A current recognised handicap certificate is requested: maximum 28 for men and 36 for women.

west-lancashire.tagline: Founded in 1873 at Blundellsands, at the southern end of the coast
west-lancashire.description:
West Lancashire Golf Club was founded in 1873 at Blundellsands, at the southern end of the Sefton Coast. The entrance is 50 yards from Hall Road station, on the line between Liverpool Central and Southport.

The club hosted Final Qualifying for The Open from 2023 to 2026 on behalf of The R&A, and hosts R&A and England Golf competitions. Visitors book online. From November 2026 to February 2027 the weekday green fee is £120 per person, with tea or coffee and a bacon roll on arrival.
west-lancashire.visitorPolicy: Visitors book online. The club publishes weekday and weekend rates for each season.

southport-ainsdale.tagline: Founded in 1906; Ryder Cup venue in 1933 and 1937
southport-ainsdale.description:
Southport & Ainsdale, known locally as S&A, was founded in 1906 and hosted the Ryder Cup in 1933 and 1937. The club says The R&A continues to choose it for the Amateur Championship.

The course sits between Hillside and Formby, among coastal dunes and heathland with gorse and heather. Visitors are welcome all year. The club shows its green fees on its online booking portal, where rates vary with demand, time of day and season.
southport-ainsdale.visitorPolicy: Visitors welcome all year. Groups of more than 12 contact the club's golf coordinator.

southport-old-links.tagline: Nine holes with 18 different tees, in Churchtown, Southport
southport-old-links.description:
Southport Old Links is in Churchtown, on the northern edge of Southport. It is a nine-hole course with 18 different tees. Golfers can book 18 holes or nine.

The club celebrates its centenary in 2026. Visitors can book tee times on weekdays and Saturdays, online up to seven days ahead. For bookings further ahead, the club asks golfers to contact its office on 01704 228207 (option 5).
southport-old-links.visitorPolicy: Visitors book tee times on weekdays and Saturdays, online up to seven days ahead.
